title: Personal Pronouns
sourceNote: The auto-captions are heavily garbled; names and sentences were reconstructed from context.
objectives: I can name all personal pronouns in the nominative
I can choose between du, ihr and Sie when speaking to people
I can use er, sie and es for people and things
I can replace a noun with the right pronoun

expressions.de: Michael wohnt in London. Er wohnt in London.
expressions.en: Michael lives in London. He lives in London.

expressions.de: Das Buch ist alt. Es ist alt.
expressions.en: The book is old. It is old.

patterns.ex: Michaela wohnt in Paris. Sie wohnt in Paris.
patterns.en: Michaela lives in Paris. She lives in Paris.

grammar.title: What is a personal pronoun?
grammar.body: A personal pronoun **replaces a noun**. It makes sentences shorter and avoids repeating the same noun. German pronouns depend on three things: the **person** (1st = I/we, 2nd = you, 3rd = he/she/it/they), **singular or plural**, and the **gender** of the noun. They are used for people and for things.
grammar.ar: الضمير الشخصي يحلّ محلّ الاسم ويمنع تكراره.

grammar.title: All pronouns (nominative)
grammar.body: In the second person you must decide between the informal *du / ihr* (friends, family, children, first names) and the formal **Sie** (strangers, official situations). *Sie* (you) is always written with a capital S, also in the middle of a sentence.

grammar.title: Examples for each person
grammar.body: First person: *ich* = only me, *wir* = me and others. Second person: *du* for one friend, *ihr* for several friends, *Sie* for one or more people you address formally. Third person: *er* replaces a masculine person, *sie* a feminine person, *es* a neuter noun, and plural *sie* replaces more than one person or thing.

examples.en: Max, do you live in Cologne? (one friend)

examples.de: Julia und Peter, wohnt ihr in Köln?
examples.en: Julia and Peter, do you live in Cologne? (two friends)

examples.de: Herr Müller, wohnen Sie in Köln?
examples.en: Mr Müller, do you live in Cologne? (formal)

examples.de: Herr und Frau Müller, wohnen Sie in Köln?
examples.en: Mr and Mrs Müller, do you live in Cologne? (formal, plural)

grammar.title: Replacing nouns: er, sie, es
grammar.body: Michael is masculine, so *Michael* becomes **er**. Michaela is feminine, so she becomes **sie**. *Das Buch* is neuter, so it becomes **es**. Petra and Jürgen (more than one person) become plural **sie**. Note that *sie* can mean *she* or *they*: the verb shows which one (*sie wohnt* = she lives; *sie wohnen* = they live).

examples.de: Michael wohnt in London. Er wohnt in London.
examples.en: Michael lives in London. He lives in London.

examples.de: Michaela wohnt in Paris. Sie wohnt in Paris.
examples.en: Michaela lives in Paris. She lives in Paris.

examples.de: Das Buch ist alt. Es ist alt.
examples.en: The book is old. It is old.

examples.de: Petra und Jürgen wohnen in Hamburg. Sie wohnen in Hamburg.
examples.en: Petra and Jürgen live in Hamburg. They live in Hamburg.

grammar.title: Four meanings of sie / Sie
grammar.body: The word is written the same in four cases: **sie** = she, **sie** = they, **Sie** = you (formal singular) and **Sie** = you (formal plural). It is capitalised only when it means *you* (formal) or when it is the first word of a sentence. Use the verb ending and the context to tell them apart.
grammar.ar: كلمة sie/Sie لها أربعة معانٍ: هي، هم، حضرتك، حضراتكم.

examples.en: They live in Hamburg. / You live in Hamburg. (formal)

mistakes.wrong: Frau Schmidt, wohnst du in Berlin?
mistakes.right: Frau Schmidt, wohnen Sie in Berlin?
mistakes.why: Use formal *Sie* for adults you do not know well.

mistakes.wrong: Das Buch ist alt. Er ist alt.
mistakes.right: Das Buch ist alt. Es ist alt.
mistakes.why: *Das Buch* is neuter, so the pronoun is *es*.

pronunciation.tip: *sie* sounds like English 'zee'. *wir* has a short i like 'veer'. *ihr* is like 'eer' with a long vowel.

lines.de: Hallo, ich bin Maria. Ich wohne in Berlin.
lines.en: Hello, I am Maria. I live in Berlin.

lines.de: Hallo, Maria! Wir wohnen auch in Berlin.
lines.en: Hello, Maria! We also live in Berlin.

lines.de: Wer ist das? Wohnt er auch in Berlin?
lines.en: Who is that? Does he also live in Berlin?

lines.de: Nein, er wohnt in London. Aber Petra und Jürgen wohnen in Hamburg. Sie wohnen nicht in Berlin.
lines.en: No, he lives in London. But Petra and Jürgen live in Hamburg. They do not live in Berlin.

tip: When you talk to someone, first decide: one person or more, friend or stranger? That gives you du, ihr or Sie.

comprehension.q: What does a personal pronoun do?
Which pronoun do you use for one friend, and which for several friends?
comprehension.a: du for one friend, ihr for several friends.

comprehension.q: Which pronoun do you use for the formal *you*?
comprehension.a: Sie, always with a capital S.

comprehension.q: Which pronoun replaces Petra and Jürgen?

exercises.title: Replace with a pronoun
exercises.instructions: Write the pronoun that replaces the underlined noun.

Michaela wohnt in Paris. = ___ wohnt in Paris.
Das Buch ist alt. = ___ ist alt.
Petra und Jürgen wohnen in Hamburg. = ___ wohnen in Hamburg.
Anna und ich wohnen in Wien. = ___ wohnen in Wien.

exercises.title: du, ihr or Sie?
exercises.instructions: Which pronoun do you use when you speak to these people?

items.q: Your friends Julia and Peter. (du / ihr / Sie)
Frau Schmidt, a stranger. (du / ihr / Sie)
Herr and Frau Schmidt, strangers. (du / ihr / Sie)

summary: Personal pronouns replace nouns; they depend on person, number and gender.
Singular: ich, du, Sie (formal), er, sie, es. Plural: wir, ihr, Sie (formal), sie.
Use du / ihr for friends and family, and Sie for formal situations.
er, sie, es replace masculine, feminine and neuter nouns, including things.
sie = she or they; Sie = you (formal), always capital.
